title: Escalation, policy, and state Power in current times

instruction.text:

The Early 21th Century
instruction.sound: Read the text and select the correct statements.

atoms.text: On September 11, 2001, Al-Qaeda carried out terrorist attacks that destroyed the World Trade Center and damaged the Pentagon. Nearly 3,000 people were killed. The attacks shattered a sense of security for US citizens, fear of foreign influence and aggressors rose and immigration policy shifted towards a focus on national security. In 2002, Congress passed the Visa Entry Reform Act to strengthen visa screening and tracking. The Enhanced Border Security Act of the same year created the Department of Homeland Security to oversee border control and immigration in tandem.

b: Immigration policy did not change after the attacks.
++The Department of Homelands Security combined border and immigration control.
++The new policies were supposed to help to regain national security.

atoms.text: Anti-immigrant and anti-Muslim sentiment increased in the United States. Stricter immigration laws made legal entry harder, leading many to migrate without proper authorisation. By 2007, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security estimated over 11 million undocumented immigrants lived in the U.S., with more than half coming from Mexico.

Immigration today
instruction.sound: Read the text and select the correct statements.

atoms.text: In 2003, the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency was created under the Department of Homeland Security. ICE agents are authorised to carry weapons, detain individuals, and deport those who violate immigration law, but they must adhere to US law and grant due process to detained persons. They are not permitted to attack peaceful protesters and cannot enter private property without a warrant, though they can make arrests in public spaces.
atoms.sound: In 2003, the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (I.C.E.) agency was created under the Department of Homeland Security. Ice agents are authorised to carry weapons, detain individuals, and deport those who violate immigration law, but they must adhere to U.S. law and grant due process to detained persons. They are not permitted to attack peaceful protesters and cannot enter private property without a warrant, though they can make arrests in public spaces.

b: ICE is part of the police force.
++ICE agents are legally allowed to carry weapons.
ICE agents are legally allowed to enter private property.

atoms.text: President Donald Trump built his political platform on anti-immigration sentiments. In his first presidency (2017-2021) he pledged to build a wall between Mexico and the US, a plan that was never fully executed. During his second term, Congress increased ICE's funding massively through the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill Act from 9,8 Billion to 28 Billion dollars.

b: ++Trump built his following and support on anti-immigration rhetoric.
The wall to Mexico was successfully built.

atoms.text: The majority of people deported in 2025 have no criminal record. About 60-70% are deported for overstaying visas or entering without authorisation. Only about 20% had been convicted of any crime, and only some 8% were accused but not yet convicted. This data leads critics to call into question the effectiveness and security benefit of deportations especially in relation to the agency's funding and legal overreach.

atoms.text: In January 2026, the killings of the US citizen Renée Good and Alex Pretti by ICE agents in Minneapolis sparked protests in Minnesota and nationwide. The protesters and opposition recognise the unlawful activity and violence, including illegal raids on private property as a dangerous radicalisation of ICE, while the Trump administration supports it.

hint.text:
Renée Good, a 37-year-old US citizen, was fatally shot by an ICE agent on January 7, 2026 during an enforcement action in Minneapolis. Alex Pretti, also a 37-year-old US citizen and intensive care nurse, was shot by several federal agents on January 24, 2026, amid protests against ICE operations.
It is reported, that about 8 people have died in ICE-related raids only in early 2026.
